scams.name: Alanya 'Buy Drinks' Card-Skimming Bar Scam
scams.description:
You are walking along Bar Street when a friendly "local" approaches in perfect English and steers you toward a "great bar nearby." The venue looks legitimate, the drinks arrive quickly, and the evening feels ordinary.

At payment, the card terminal is brought to your table. The waiter taps the screen repeatedly saying the transaction "didn't go through." Each retry captures your card data. By the next morning your card shows €800–€2,500 in charges from bars you never entered.

Pay cash for drinks on Bar Street and watch the card terminal stay on your table without being taken away. If a terminal shows a failed transaction, refuse additional retries and pay with a different card or cash instead. Check your bank app immediately after any bar payment, and freeze the card via your bank app within seconds if unauthorized charges appear. Report the venue to Tourism Police at 155.
scams.avoidance: NEVER follow an unsolicited 'friendly local' to any bar in Alanya Pay cash for drinks at bars (small bills, never ₺500 notes) If using card, watch the terminal stay at your table; refuse 'didn't go through' retries Photograph the amount on any signed paper receipt BEFORE signing Freeze card via banking app within 60 seconds of suspected skimming
scams.location: Alanya bars on Bar Street (Damlataş Caddesi) and Cleopatra Beach promenade, side-street venues off the main strip, late-night returns from Karaalioğlu Park area
scams.tldr: Fluent-English "locals" on Alanya's Bar Street lure tourists to flagged venues where staff skim card details during fake "declined payment" retries — charging €800–€2,500 to the card overnight across multiple phantom transactions.

scams.name: Cleopatra Beach Taxi & Boat Excursion Overcharge
scams.description:
You plan a day at Cleopatra Beach — 2 km of fine sand and Alanya's most visited beach. Taxis are plentiful at the town center. A beach tout approaches the promenade offering a day boat tour for €10 per person.

The taxi driver declines to run the meter and quotes ₺500–₺800 for a ride that costs ₺140–₺200. The €10 boat tour turns out to be a two-hour trip with only two swim stops instead of the promised five, and the guide demands a ₺200 "mandatory tip" before passengers can disembark.

Insist on the taxi meter before boarding and confirm the ₺140–₺200 fare range to Cleopatra Beach; use the BiTaksi app for app-regulated fares with digital receipts. For boat tours, book through your hotel or a vetted operator at ₺600–₺900 per person including lunch. Get confirmed swim stop counts, drink prices, and a written "no mandatory tip" assurance before boarding.
scams.avoidance: Insist on meter for taxis; confirm ₺140–₺200 range to Cleopatra Beach before boarding Use BiTaksi app for app-regulated fares Book boat tours via hotel concierge or vetted operator at ₺600–₺900/person Decline beach-tout 'special tours' under €15 — the math forces shortcuts and tip demands Walk the 1.5 km coastal promenade back to Alanya center (25 min) instead of taxi
scams.location: Cleopatra Beach taxi rank, Damlataş Caddesi pickup zones, Alanya Marina boat-tour booking offices, Portacall (Liman) ferry transfers
scams.tldr: Alanya taxis to Cleopatra Beach refuse the meter and quote ₺500–₺800 for a ₺140–₺200 metered ride, while beach touts sell "special boat tours" at €10–€12 that hide mandatory ₺200 tips and deliver half the promised swim stops.

scams.name: Restaurant Pricing Inflation & 'Tourist Menu' Doubling
scams.description:
A sidewalk tout recruits you into a restaurant near the seafront. The laminated English-language menu shows appealing photos of kebabs, meze, and fish dishes — but no prices. The table is set with bread and olives before you have ordered anything.

The bill arrives 30–60% above verbal quotes. The bread and olives appear at ₺50–₺100 per item. The "fish of the day" priced "per kilo" weighs more than expected, and a cover charge (kuver) of ₺50–₺80 per person appears as a separate line item.

Walk one block back from the seafront and eat where Turkish residents eat — restaurants with Turkish-language menus and posted prices are reliably cheaper and honest. For fish, have it weighed in your presence and confirm the per-kilo price in writing before ordering. Refuse complimentary bread and meze unless prices are confirmed, and check the bill line-by-line before paying.
scams.avoidance: Walk one block off Bar Street/Cleopatra strip to find restaurants for Turkish residents Community-recommended: Köşem Restaurant (Atatürk Caddesi), Sofra (Old Town), Mahmutlar Manti House For fish, see it weighed in your presence and get per-kg price in writing Refuse complimentary bread/olives unless prices are confirmed Check bill line-by-line; dispute any item not ordered
scams.location: Restaurants on Bar Street (Damlataş Caddesi), Cleopatra Beach restaurant strip, Alanya Old Town tourist alleys, Mahmutlar all-inclusive resort area exterior
scams.tldr: Restaurants on Alanya's tourist strip serve meals with no prices on the English menu, then bill 30–60% above verbal quotes — with unordered "complimentary" bread, meze, and cover charges adding ₺150–₺250 per person to the total.

scams.name: Antalya (AYT) & Gazipaşa (GZP) Airport Transfer Overcharge
scams.description:
You land at Antalya Airport (AYT) — the main gateway for Alanya, 130 km to the east — and head toward the exits. Unofficial operators in the arrivals hall call out "Alanya? Fixed price €120, very fast." Most package-holiday travelers also see their tour operator's shuttle boarding point nearby.

The legitimate metered taxi fare from AYT to central Alanya runs ₺2,000–₺2,500 (€50–€63). Unofficial operators charge €100–€150 for the same trip and refuse the meter. From the smaller Gazipaşa-Alanya Airport (GZP, 40 km east), the legitimate metered fare is ₺600–₺900 (€15–€22); touts there charge €40–€60.

If your package-tour operator includes a free coach transfer, confirm the meeting point before landing and use it — it is the cheapest, most overcharge-proof option. For independent travelers, the Havaş airport bus runs from AYT to Alanya otogar for ₺250 per person (~€6.50). If taking a taxi, confirm the ₺2,000–₺2,500 range upfront and insist on Tarife 1 (day rate) before boarding. Uber does not operate in Alanya; only BiTaksi and licensed taxis are legitimate.
scams.avoidance: Confirm package-tour transfer is included with TUI/Jet2/Tez Tour/Anex Tour before arrival From AYT, take Havaş bus to Alanya otogar (₺250, 2.5 hr) for budget independent travel If using metered taxi from AYT, confirm ₺2,000–₺2,500 range and insist on Tarife 1 Book Welcome Pickups for AYT-to-Alanya (€60–€80 per car for 4) Pre-book late-night Bar Street returns through hotel reception
scams.location: Antalya Airport (AYT) taxi rank, Gazipaşa-Alanya Airport (GZP) taxi rank, hotel-concierge transfers, late-night returns from Bar Street nightlife
scams.tldr: Unofficial transfer operators at Antalya Airport quote €100–€150 for the 130-km drive to Alanya that legitimately costs ₺2,000–₺2,500 (€50–€63) on the meter, while GZP operators charge €40–€60 for a ₺600–₺900 metered ride.

scams.name: All-Inclusive Resort Excursion Reseller & Hotel Tout Markups
scams.description:
You ask the hotel concierge about day trips to Manavgat Waterfall, Side Ancient City, or Aspendos Theatre. They offer a polished brochure with a bus, lunch, and a full day's program for €80 per person. The price seems reasonable.

The excursion includes two or three "demonstration" stops at onyx jewelry, Turkish delight, and carpet showrooms — each with 30–40 minutes of high-pressure sales and the operator earning a 30–40% commission on purchases. The stops cannot be skipped; the bus waits at each one. Actual sightseeing fills only half the day.

Book excursions directly via GetYourGuide or Viator with the "no shopping stops" filter, and verify TÜRSAB licensing before paying. A legitimate Manavgat Waterfall + Side day-trip costs €30–€50 per person through vetted small-group operators. For Alanya Castle and Cleopatra Beach, no excursion is needed — both are walkable from central Alanya hotels.
scams.avoidance: Avoid hotel-concierge excursion sales (commission-driven referrals) Book directly via GetYourGuide or Viator with 'no shopping stops' filter and TÜRSAB licensing verified Manavgat + Side day-trip should be €30–€50 per person at vetted operators For Aspendos, hire a private driver (€80–€120 round-trip for up to 4) instead of bus tours If tour stops at 'demonstration' or 'cooperative,' stay on the bus and refuse to enter
scams.location: All-inclusive hotel concierge desks (Mahmutlar, Avsallar, Konaklı), beach-promenade tour booking offices, hotel-arranged 'special excursion' packages
scams.tldr: Hotel concierges and promenade tour offices in Alanya sell €60–€120 "all-inclusive excursions" to Manavgat Waterfall and Side that hide two or three compulsory shopping stops where the operator earns 30–40% commissions.

scams.name: Damlataş Cave & Castle 'Skip-the-Line' Tout Scams
scams.description:
You arrive at the entrance to Damlataş Cave or Alanya Castle. A man near the gate says the official ticket window is "closed today" or that a "special combined pass" is required for entry. He produces a set of tickets and names a price.

Official entry prices are ₺120 (~€3) for Damlataş Cave, ₺240 (~€6) for Alanya Castle, and ₺120 for the Red Tower. The tout's "skip-the-line" tickets cost €15–€25 per person for the same access. None of these attractions has meaningful queues except briefly during cruise ship mornings when several hundred visitors arrive at once.

Walk past all touts directly to the official ticket booth at each attraction — the booth is never "closed" during operating hours. The cable car to the castle (₺200 round-trip) is the practical option for the steep climb. For a Castle + Cable Car + Damlataş Cave visit, the total official cost is under €15 per person. Buy water and snacks at a Migros before the climb — castle vendors charge three times the street price.
scams.avoidance: Walk past all touts to the official ticket booth at each attraction Damlataş Cave ₺120, Alanya Castle ₺240, Red Tower ₺120, Cable Car ₺200 round-trip — all official prices under €6 Combined experience under €15 per person paid at official booths Decline 'skip-the-line' offers — these attractions rarely have queues Buy water, snacks, evil-eye souvenirs at Migros before the climb
scams.location: Damlataş Cave entrance area, Alanya Castle (Alanya Kalesi) approach paths, cable-car queue, Red Tower (Kızıl Kule) ticket area
scams.tldr: Touts at Alanya Castle and Damlataş Cave tell tourists the ticket booth is "closed" or a "special bundle pass" is needed, then sell unofficial tickets at €15–€25 for attractions that cost ₺120–₺240 at the official booth.
